title: Screen spec
description: A screen described in terms of THIS design system, agreed before any code is written. Validated by scripts/check-screen-spec.mjs against component-registry.json.

_why.description: A note about a non-obvious decision the fields cannot carry.

implementation.description: Repo-relative path to the screen this spec describes — or a LIST of paths when the screen splits into modules, read as one screen. Optional: a spec is written before the screen exists. Once set, check:spec verifies the files really use the template and the components named here, so the spec stops being a wish and becomes a claim that can be wrong.

_templateNote.description: Why the named template is not (yet) the one the implementation uses.

project.description: The app this screen belongs to (the apps/<name> folder). Optional once `implementation` is set — the path says it then. It matters BEFORE the code exists: a content model traces its screens by project, and a spec with neither project nor implementation is invisible to that check.

title.description: Screen name as a person would say it.

goal.description: What the user is here to do. One sentence, no feature list.

primaryQuestion.description: The question the user asks first when this screen opens. The screen answers it before anything else: the first zone that declares `answers` must answer exactly this question, which is what makes 'the answer comes first' checkable rather than a hope.

audience.description: Who operates the screen. Experts switch fast and want density (GOV.UK's documented exception); public users get one thing at a time. Some selection rules read this.

archetype.description: What KIND of screen this is, from the taxonomy in screen-specs/README.md (backbone: SAP Fiori floorplans). list = find-and-act over a filterable set; worklist = process a given queue (no filter bar — having one means the archetype is list); detail = one record in full; hub = entry points to other places; overview = glance across sources, action happens elsewhere. The archetype constrains the template and check-screen-spec.mjs verifies the pairing.

template.description: A block from src/blocks (ListPageTemplate, DetailPageTemplate, AuthTemplate, FormModal), or "custom" with customReason filled in.

customReason.description: Required when template is "custom": why no existing block fits. This is the escalation point, not a shortcut.

zones.description: The screen's regions, in reading order.

task.description: What the user DOES in this zone, one verb. The collection tasks (find, compare, scan, browse, monitor, analyze, process, navigate) trigger the representation rules in selection-rules.json; read, input and act do not. This is the judgment the spec review approves — the gate then holds the components to it.

data.description: The shape of what this zone shows. Required as soon as the zone has a collection task and a collection representation, because the rules cannot fire on adjectives.

item.description: What one item is: structured fields (record), text to read (prose), an image or preview that carries the decision (visual), a number on a scale (metric).

cardinality.description: How many items. unbounded forbids Table (DataGrid virtualizes).

fields.description: How many attributes per item actually matter to the task. 4+ comparable fields is what earns columns.

editable.description: true only when editing values IS the task, which demands DataGrid. Occasional inline edits on a table do not set this.

answers.description: The question this zone answers, in the words of primaryQuestion where it is that one. Zones are in reading order, so the order of `answers` is the order the screen answers questions in — and the first one must be the primaryQuestion.

surface.description: When this zone is on screen: page zones are always visible together, each tab:<name> is its own context beside the page, a dialog covers the rest. Drives the one-primary-action check: two primaries on one surface are side by side and get named. Default: page, except a zone named "dialogs", which defaults to dialog.

components.description: Registry components used here. Props may be pinned as "Button variant=primary".

states.description: What the screen looks like when it is not the happy path. Every state names the component that renders it.

data.description: The records the screen shows and where they come from. Mock is a valid source; say so.

openQuestions.description: What the spec cannot answer yet. Empty is a claim, not a default.

acceptance.description: What makes THIS screen succeed, as short yes/no statements a reviewer (human or judge) can verify by looking — not restatements of global rules the gate already checks. Per-screen criteria measurably beat a universal checklist (the SALT ablation: dropping them cost 17%); these are the rubric the future judge lane will score against, written while the intent is fresh rather than reconstructed later.

behaviours.description: What the screen DOES, in the words the requirement was written in. The zones above say what it is made of; these say what has to remain true about it. Each one names the test that proves it, and check:spec fails when a named test does not exist or does not claim the scenario, so a behaviour cannot be agreed to and then quietly not built.

id.description: Short, stable, unique within this spec. It is the string a test carries to claim this scenario.

given.description: The state of the world before, in plain language.

then.description: What must be true after. One observable outcome, not a list.

why.description: The requirement this comes from. A scenario with no why is a test looking for a reason.

provenBy.description: Repo-relative path to the test file that proves it. The test must carry `<specId>#<id>` in its name, which is what makes the link machine-checkable rather than a claim in prose.

pendingReason.description: Why this is agreed and not yet proven. Allowed instead of provenBy, counted as debt and printed on every run — never a way to keep it quiet.
